questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted to study in an English speaking country, since all research are made in English. I then wanted a city or country I would feel safe in, and believed would be a good fit. So I wanted to go to Canada, but I did not have the grades. My brothers girlfriend told me about her visit to Boston and I thought that Boston sounded like a great city, so I applied.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I have experienced SO much, but it did not meet my expectations. The US was not a great fit for me. I had a lot of trouble adjusting to the American way, and I was lonely a lot of the time. It was very difficult to find friends, since they dont make friends the same way as we do in Europe. I am grateful for all the amazing experiences I have had, but if I had to chose again, I would go somewhere else.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fine. You had a contact person, who was a big help if you did not understand or could not find the information you needed. Once you had your BU account, it was okay to navigate the systems. They are a lot like the systems at KU. Also you had to take some online courses that explained the systems, and how the american education system works.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None really. You were pretty much left all by your self. When I checked in to my dorm, the resident assistant helped me understand how the building worked, and said I could always ask for help if I needed it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I thought it was very helpful all the online classes I could take from home, so I wasn't blindsided when I arrived. Though I am very disappointed that no one showed us (exchange students) around, or made any get togethers for all of the exchange students. You just arrived, and then you had to find everything on your own, even someone to talk to.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: At BU you are guarantied housing through the university if you want it. I lived in a normal dorm style room, so 2 people sharing a small room with no kitchen. You also shared bathroom with the whole floor. But you could apply for other types of housing if you wanted to have a kitchen or a bathroom only shared with 2-3 other people. But the dorm style was the cheapest.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Most did not have their own kitchen, so you had to have a dining plan. There are 3 big dining halls, where you can eat all you want after you have entered. Depending on the dining plan you selected you had a certain amount of meals you could eat in these dining halls. You also had some dining point, you could use at Starbucks and other small cafés on campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is expensive!!!!! You can save a lot of money by living of campus, but it is harder to meet the other exchange students, because most lives on campus. We usually met in the dining halls to eat together. Also you can be very unlucky not to find any great housing off campus, if you dont look in good time.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The housing on campus varied a lot in its quality. My dorm was okay, but one of the other dorms (Warren Towers) was so disgusting. If you apply for on campus housing, go for apartment style, suit style or smaller dorms.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found it quit difficult to find the classes i wanted, that was open. Also i got my BU login too late, so most classes was already full. But when I arrived i could just change classes, because there is an add/drop period.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to find the classes you thought sounded interesting in the BU course catalog. Then you registered for the classes on student link (their website for students). You could always change your registration until the add/drop period ended.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could write to your contact person.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: At first I did not get any of the classes I wanted, but then later I got two of the classes, just by writing checking student link often, but also by being on the waitlist. It was actually really great that I did not get the classes I wanted to begin with, because it got me to expand my search, and I found a course I ended up really loving. It was the best course I had.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Spend time before registration begins on finding all the classes you might be interested in. The more the better, and then register the minute you can. Keep checking student link if you did not get a spot the first time, because many are making changes to their schedule right before classes starts.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really liked my classes and my professors. I really felt like I learned a lot. Even though there was a lot of repetition, I still learned the same in different ways and in different perspectives.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As an undergrad you can take up till 500 level courses, and please do. They are not too hard, and they have smaller classes, so it is easier to meet people and get to know your professor. I had two 500 level courses and one 300 level course. The biggest different was that you got more help in the 300 level course. It wasn't easier per say, but it felt like you had training wheels and the professor held your hand more. It actually made the work load bigger because you couldn't manage your own time as much.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In my 500 level courses it was like gymnasium. Class learning instead if big lectures. In my 300 level course it was big lectures and lab. There was no class discussions or task solving classes. The professor who was in charge of the course chose what type of teaching they wanted to teach. They have more creative freedom than the professors at KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
CAS BI 513 - Genetics Lab
CAS BI 572 - Advanced Genetics
CAS BI 311 - General Microbiology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them! I really loved Advanced genetics. We learned about different model organisms and how they are used in research, so you really got to think about experiments and how you got the results you wanted and which methods to use. I also really loved General Microbiology, because it provided me with a greater knowledge on how the world works. Microbes are so important for the world and for us humans. I feel it is important to know the basics about microbes in order to fully understand diseases and research of diseases.

Housing DKK per month *

Personal spending DKK per month *

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None really. But I did end up using a lot of money on food. Also trains are expensive, so if you plan on going away much, you have to order the tickets in great time.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing, dining plan and US insurance was VERY expensive. 60.000kr for 4 months. Also eating out isn't as cheap as it used to be. But cloth and stuff for your room was cheap enough. Amazon is AMAZING!!!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not join any clubs, but BU has their own fitness center, called fitrec.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So so many. They have a big meeting on the football field in the begining of the semester, where you can meet all the clubs and join if you want.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I had two PDP classes, yoga and Hiphop. They where held in fitrec, which was free for BU students. FitRec is HUGE. They have everything you want for every sport you may play.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Just see Boston! It is an amazing city. Walk the freedom trail and see the public garden. See Quincy market and little italy. If you have the time, then hike the blue mountains.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Not really. They have very strict alcohol laws, so you cannot drink in public and all events are without alcohol, which was very strange to me. Also most people you meet are under the age of 21, so they cannot drink, which makes them feel more immature then 18-19 years old do in Denmark. Also everything is sweet, and they do no care about quality of the food they eat.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Yes, join a club. any club. They is the only way you meet people. Also try reaching out to the other exchange students. You have to be very open and "agressive" in order to meet people. You ask people you meet for a cup of coffee or if they want to eat lunch. It is very strange to that open and straight forward, but you have to if you want to meet people. Also try to meet with the other danes back home before going over there, so you are not totally alone.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Their alcohol culture as explained. Also their healthcare system.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: You can customize everything which i really like. Also they care a lot about sports, so I went to see many ice hockey games, basketball games and so on. That culture is really fun. supporting your own university and spend every weekend with seeing some sport, mostly ice hockey.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared for how expensive it is! 
BU makes nothing social for the exchange student, so you have to be very straight forward and open if you want any friends. 
Take every opportunity you get. See the sports games, go the the festival or whatever happens that week. Read BU today that is sent to your email for inspiration on what to do that weekend.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Go to every class, even though your grades do not matter. If you are behind from the beginning, then it is hard to relax in the end. Also check out Boston Collage before you decide. BU is right next to the city, so it is easy to experience Boston, but campus is so boring and long. Boston collage is smaller and prettier, however it is further out. But there are trains and Uber/Lyft. Also you spend so much time on campus, so you have to make sure it is a place you actually like. I was very disappointed when I first saw BU campus, because it is not like Harvard. It is a city campus, and looks like it.
Also BU has its own pub, called BU pub. It is very cozy, so make sure to check it out. also it is a great way to meet people your own age.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Seeing Boston, New York and New England in general. I have always wanted to see the east coast. Also I feel like you have a certain view of USA here in Europe, but it is different to experience first hand how the country is. I have a new understanding of USA.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding friends! I felt lonely most of the time, because I had so much free time. I was used to have a job and a volunteer job, so when I all of a sudden had to fill my day with other things, it was hard. Also you cannot expect the same few people to be with you every day of the week.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: It was a great experience that I do not regret, but it was not the easiest place to live. Just really think about what you want from your experience.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
